prayerExcerpt.en-US: In the love of his flock and his zeal for their salvation he was infirm with the infirm, and wept with those that wept.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: No amor de seu rebanho e em seu zelo pela salvação deles, era enfermo com os enfermos, e chorava com os que choravam.

meta.face: A Leinsterman of about eighty with a fair, pink, soft complexion and a SHORT, BROAD face, ROUND at the jaw — the front of the head shaved from ear to ear in the Irish tonsure, leaving a broad, high forehead, with fine white hair falling behind the ears; a BROAD, fleshy nose with a ROUNDED tip, WIDE-SET, moist, gentle blue-grey eyes whose inner brows are LIFTED in COMPASSION, soft, full cheeks, a small, tender mouth; a FULL, SOFT, WAVY WHITE beard reaching the breast; the look of one who weeps with those who weep. Not columba (clean-shaven, broad and ruddy), the long, narrow, receding-chinned finbarr, the long, big-boned columban, the compact, square gall, the heavy-browed david_wales, the smooth, clean-shaven malachi_armagh or valery on the same day (lean, narrow, short brown beard).
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The compassionate face follows the book ('he was infirm with the infirm, and wept with those that wept'); the white beard and the crozier follow the statue at Clonard on English Wikipedia; the Irish tonsure is the one on the other Irish monks' cards. The school of monks follows the Martyrology ('padre e maestro di una grande schiera di monaci') and Santi e Beati's notice ('maestro dei santi d'Irlanda').
